_doc: Single source of truth for §10-V Banned-vocab spec ↔ banned-vocab.patterns mapping. tests/scripts/spec-pattern-drift.test.js validates both sides against this manifest. Adding a new pattern to hooks/banned-vocab.patterns OR a new banned term to spec §10-V REQUIRES updating an entry here, otherwise CI red. v0.7.1 R-N1 (drift test). The fixture is intentionally explicit (no regex auto-extraction): legibility on review > clever parsing. Fields per entry — term: the spec-listed phrase or the literal pattern body; category: one of EN-adj / EN-hedge / EN-ratio / ZH-adj / ZH-ratio; in_spec: true if §10-V text contains `term` verbatim; pattern: the regex from banned-vocab.patterns this entry is enforced by, null if exempt; exempt_reason: required when in_spec=false OR pattern=null; note: optional clarification. SINCE v6.21.2 (plugin 0.55.0): spec §10-V is compressed to OK-shapes + pointers, so every entry is in_spec=false / pattern-enforced; the prose enumeration lives in reference_banned_vocab_examples.md. Ten former spec-only terms with no pattern (likely / arguably / most of the time / usually passes / often fails / 通常如此 / 一般来说 / 大部分情况 / 大多数时候 / 多数情况下 — all 'too common in legitimate language') were retired from this fixture (drift-6 would count them as vestigial); they remain documented in the reference memory file.
